item.title: Lyft is paying $272.5M to settle lawsuit over how it classified drivers
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Today, gig economy drivers are classified as contractors. This settlement clears up a lingering lawsuit from 2020 when that was still an unanswered issue.

item.title: Kevin Mandia’s new ‘agent swarm’ security startup Armadin raises $255.5M at $2.5B valuation
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Kevin Mandia, best known as the founder of Mandiant, has a new startup that is using agent swarms to test and protect enterprises.

item.title: Musk’s AI chatbot Grok reportedly encouraged Trump to capture Venezuela’s president
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: President Trump reportedly asked for Grok's opinion before invading Venezuela and capturing Nicolás Maduro.

item.title: ChatGPT can now virtually try on clothes for you
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: OpenAI is rolling out new shopping features for ChatGPT that let users virtually try on clothing and accessories using their own photos and save products they like to a Favorites library.

item.title: Google thinks SpaceX’s Starship has to launch 1,800 times before space data centers get off the ground
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: Google launched its first advanced chip into orbit to pave the way for space data centers.

item.title: World’s first enhanced geothermal power plant completed in just 23 months
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Fervo Energy completed its first power plant in less than two years. The next phases promise to connect to the grid even quicker.

item.title: OpenAI cuts ties with 3 safety researchers, WSJ reports
item.dc:creator: Aditya Mehta
item.description: OpenAI has parted ways with three safety researchers after an internal investigation found they mishandled sensitive company information, report says.

item.title: Opus 5.5 loves to tell you ‘this matters’ (and other AI writing tells)
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: Opus 5.5’s biggest tell is the word “dependable,” which pops up 23 times more often than in human samples.

item.title: This startup wants to turn idle car inventory into rental revenue
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: When Igor Dobrianskyi looks at a car dealership lot, he doesn't see rows of cars — he sees millions of dollars just sitting there, depreciating. Come see MyMonthlyCar in the Startup Battlefield 200 at TechCrunch Disrupt, taking place October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.

item.title: Amazon releases its own Jev clone as decision models flood the web
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: Amazon Web Services' Strand Labs has released the latest Jevalike decision model, Strands Decider 2B.

item.title: Shopify debuts Canvas, a way to build online stores by chatting with AI
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Shopify’s new Canvas site builder lets merchants create and customize their online stores by chatting with its AI agent Sidekick, while watching the changes happen in real time.

item.title: California governor vetoes bill banning use of ‘pervert glasses’ to secretly record people
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The California state bill would have penalized people who secretly recorded people in public with wearables equipped with cameras and microphones.

item.title: One year later, Tesla and Musk still don’t have a good definition of ‘abundance’
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The CEO promised to get more specific about his vision. But the details are still absent.

item.title: Brian Chesky interview: AI agents need their own operating system
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Brian Chesky on making Airbnb agent-friendly, the state of consumer AI, and why the world needs an AI-native operating system.

item.title: Photon held a funeral for mobile apps. Now it has $4.5M to help replace them with agents.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: The startup helps developers build AI agents that work over iMessage, SMS/RCS, email, and other messaging platforms. It's a bet that consumers will increasingly use agents instead of downloading apps.

item.title: Hearing tech startup Legato launches its AI hearing glasses
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: The glasses stem from the startup’s goal of making hearing care more accessible by addressing the cost, comfort, and stigma associated with traditional hearing aids.

item.title: Audible’s new features let you explore book worlds — and use AI to talk to characters
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Audible is rolling out new features that help listeners keep track of characters, explore places and imagery mentioned in books, and even interact with characters using generative AI.

item.title: The new Kindle ditches the raised bezel in a push toward a smaller, lighter e-reader
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: The new Kindle lineup features its lightest and thinnest designs yet, with a sleek, front-flush display that eliminates bezels for good.

item.title: Amazon introduces Kindle Click, a $35 remote for turning pages
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: The compact Bluetooth remote is designed to let readers turn pages without touching their Kindle.

item.title: Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, raises $8M to run AI on satellites
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.
